business_process: 911 emergency call processing and dispatch (RCC-1 to RCC-3)
description: Receive CAD-to-CAD incidents and transferred callers from 26 county PSAPs; triage with the emergency medical dispatch protocol; recommend and assign the closest unit; track units to hospital
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Delayed ambulance response can contribute to death or disability; about 6,200 responses a day across 23 counties; county agreements set response-time standards with penalties; manual dispatch at full volume stays safe for about 2 hours
manual_workaround: Manual dispatch: paper incident cards and unit status boards; county P25 radio; PSAP voice-announces new calls; center-to-center failover (RCC-1 and RCC-2 tested; RCC-3 not tested)
dependent_systems: SYS-01; SYS-04; SYS-06; SYS-07; SYS-08; SYS-11
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; CAD software vendor; county PSAPs; county P25 radio systems; carriers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Dispatchers (about 760 at RCC-1 to RCC-3); communications center supervisors; field crews
quantified_impact_basis: Late-response penalties under county agreements (about $0.6 million), overtime and mutual-aid costs (about $0.9 million), and 911 transports lost or billed late because incident data is incomplete (about $0.9 million)
single_points_of_failure: Single CAD instance (standby region warm, failover measured at 1 h 25 min against a 1 h RTO)

description: Same process as BP-01 on AQ-01's legacy on-premises CAD until migration to the enterprise CAD (due 2027-03-31)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same life-safety drivers as BP-01; about 680 responses a day; the legacy CAD backs up nightly (actual RPO 24 h) and has never been restore-tested
manual_workaround: Manual dispatch binder at RCC-4; county radio; no center-to-center failover until the CAD migration
dependent_third_parties: Legacy CAD vendor; local IT support firm; 4 county PSAPs
quantified_impact_basis: County penalties, overtime, and lost or late-billed 911 transports at the AQ-01 counties
single_points_of_failure: Legacy CAD server (single instance, unsupported operating system, no tested restore)

business_process: Interfacility and non-emergency transport scheduling and dispatch
description: Book trips from about 300 hospitals and 1,900 facilities; schedule crews; dispatch and track (about 2,200 trips a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: About 45% of ground revenue (about $2.6 million a day); delayed hospital discharges and missed dialysis or oncology appointments; hospital transport agreements set response windows
manual_workaround: Phone and fax booking to a paper schedule; defer non-urgent trips; tell facilities the expected delay
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider A; CAD software vendor; telephony platform vendor
quantified_impact_basis: About 40% of interfacility revenue deferred or lost to other providers, plus service credits under hospital agreements

business_process: Field communications, AVL, and mobile data
description: Mobile data to MDCs, AVL positions for unit recommendation, status changes, and navigation; county P25 radio is the life-safety voice channel
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Without AVL, dispatchers cannot pick the closest unit; without MDCs, all status traffic moves to radio and slows dispatch
manual_workaround: Radio status reports; dispatchers estimate unit positions from the status board; paper maps in each ambulance
dependent_third_parties: Cellular carriers; vehicle router management service; county P25 radio systems
quantified_impact_basis: Slower responses (penalty exposure) and radio congestion overtime
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 fleet on separate routers and the legacy CAD
single_points_of_failure: Vehicle router management service (single SaaS); primary cellular carrier for 160 single-carrier routers

business_process: Patient care documentation and hospital record delivery (ePCR)
description: Crews document care on ePCR tablets; records go to the receiving hospital and to each state's EMS data system
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: State rules require a patient care record for the receiving hospital (Florida worked example: on request within 48 hours of dispatch, Rule 64J-1.014, F.A.C.); tablets work offline; about 5,200 records a day
manual_workaround: Paper patient care records in every ambulance; back-entry within 48 hours; verbal hand-off at the hospital
quantified_impact_basis: Back-entry overtime and claims held until records are complete
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 moved onto the enterprise ePCR in 2026-05

description: Cardiac monitors send 12-lead ECGs through the monitor vendor's cloud relay so hospitals can activate the cardiac team before arrival
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Pre-arrival activation shortens time to treatment for heart attacks; about 450 transmissions a day
manual_workaround: Voice report by phone or radio with the crew's interpretation; hospital reads the printout on arrival
dependent_third_parties: Cardiac monitor vendor cloud relay; hospitals
quantified_impact_basis: Small direct cost; the safety impact dominates

description: Shift schedules for about 8,200 field clinicians; EMT and paramedic certification and driver checks before a shift
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Printed two-week schedules cover short outages; staffing a unit with a lapsed certification is a licensing violation
manual_workaround: Printed schedules; supervisors confirm credentials from the last exported roster
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime from manual scheduling and unfilled shifts
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 crews moved to enterprise scheduling 2026-07

description: Import trips from ePCR, code service level and mileage, attach certification statements, submit claims, post payments
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Cash: about $5.75 million a day of ground transport revenue; payers accept late claims within filing limits; Medicare documentation rules (42 CFR 410.40(e); 424.516(f))
manual_workaround: Queue claims; submit high-value claims through payer portals; move volume to the secondary clearinghouse
dependent_third_parties: Revenue cycle platform vendor; primary clearinghouse (about 75% of claims); secondary clearinghouse; banks
quantified_impact_basis: Collections delayed about $5.75 million per day of outage; borrowing cost about $25,000 per day of delay (fictional credit facility rate)

description: Receive and attach physician certification statements (PCS) and facility face sheets to trips
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Medicare requires certification statements on file for non-emergency transports (42 CFR 410.40(e)); claims wait for documents
manual_workaround: Facilities fax PCS to the billing center's backup fax line; staff attach later
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-05 document capture; cloud fax
quantified_impact_basis: Claims held for missing PCS; rework

business_process: EMS billing services for public agencies (SL-1)
description: Claims, payment posting, and reporting for 46 public EMS agencies (about 610,000 claims a year)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Client agreements set claim-submission and reporting turnaround and availability commitments; the company is each agency's business associate; SOC 2 commitments (P09)
manual_workaround: Queue client claims; daily status notice to agencies; prioritize Medicare and Medicaid claims at filing deadlines
dependent_systems: SYS-03; SYS-04; SL-1 client portal (Cloud provider A)
quantified_impact_basis: About $410,000 billing services revenue per day plus service credits under client agreements
acquired_operation_dependency: 9 of the 46 agencies came with AQ-02 (migrated 2026-08)

business_process: Managed transportation trip intake and scheduling (SL-2)
description: Members and facilities book NEMT trips by phone, app, or portal; the platform verifies eligibility and assigns network providers (about 19,700 trips a day)
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Members miss dialysis, chemotherapy, and other recurring care; state Medicaid and plan contracts set call answer and trip assignment standards with penalties
manual_workaround: Standing orders for recurring trips are pre-assigned 72 hours ahead and printed; contact centers take urgent requests on paper and phone providers
dependent_systems: Managed transportation platform (Cloud provider B); SYS-11; SYS-04
dependent_third_parties: Cloud provider B; telephony platform vendor; state Medicaid eligibility interfaces; network providers
dependent_people_or_facilities: Contact center agents (about 1,050); network operations staff
quantified_impact_basis: Contract performance penalties and replacement trips (about $0.9 million a day); most revenue is capitated, so the exposure is penalties and member harm, not lost revenue
single_points_of_failure: Managed transportation platform (single region with warm standby)

business_process: Network provider payments and encounter reporting (SL-2)
description: Validate completed trips, pay about 1,400 network providers, and submit encounter data to Medicaid agencies and plans
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Small network providers depend on weekly payments; encounter data deadlines are monthly under the contracts
manual_workaround: Pay providers on the prior week's amount and true up later
dependent_third_parties: Banks; state and plan encounter interfaces
quantified_impact_basis: Provider complaints and late-payment terms under network agreements

description: Request lines, transferred 911 callers, facility lines, contact center routing, and call recording
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Transferred 911 callers and request lines cannot reach dispatch; recordings are evidence and quality records
manual_workaround: Forward numbers to backup carrier and supervisor phones; PSAPs relay caller information by radio
dependent_third_parties: Telephony and contact center platform vendor; carriers
quantified_impact_basis: Lost interfacility bookings, contact center penalties, and overtime
single_points_of_failure: Telephony and contact center platform (single SaaS)

description: Biweekly payroll for 12,000 employees (about $30 million per run); SOX-relevant
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll cutoff 72 hours before pay date; wage payment laws; retention of field staff
manual_workaround: Repeat the prior payroll with adjustments through the payroll provider
quantified_impact_basis: Manual adjustments and penalties if payroll is late

description: Quarterly and annual close, SOX controls, 10-Q and 10-K preparation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines at quarter-end (MTD drops to 48 hours during the close window); SOX IT general controls
manual_workaround: Extend the close calendar; manual journal entries with dual approval
quantified_impact_basis: Overtime and audit fees; a late filing would be Severe

description: Vehicle maintenance, readiness checks, and medication and controlled substance inventory at 12 fleet hubs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Ambulances out of service reduce coverage after about 2 days; controlled substance records must stay accurate
manual_workaround: Paper readiness checklists and controlled substance logs; phone orders to distributors
quantified_impact_basis: Expedite fees and units out of service after day 2

description: State EMS data submissions and monthly county response-time compliance reports
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: State data can be submitted late with notice; county reports are monthly; data comes from CAD and ePCR backups
manual_workaround: Submit late with an explanation; rebuild reports from restored data
quantified_impact_basis: Staff time; small contract exposure if county reports are late
acquired_operation_dependency: AQ-01 county reports are built by hand from the legacy CAD
regulatory_driver: Rule 64J-1.014, F.A.C. (Florida worked example); county agreements
